intro: Convert pressure in Pa (Pascals) to pounds per square inch (psi) accurately for HVAC static pressure, vacuum systems, hydraulic engineering, and meteorology. Under NIST and SI standards, 1 psi equals 6,894.75729 Pascals, so 1 Pa equals 0.00014504 psi—divide Pascals by 6,894.75729, or tap Swap to switch to a PSI to Pa converter. Check pressure benchmarks from 1 Pa to 10,000,000 Pa below.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Gauge (psig) vs. Absolute (psia) & Pascal Prefix Scaling (Pa, kPa, MPa)
items: Tire and air-compressor gauges show gauge pressure (psig, referenced to local air pressure), while vacuum and gas-law calculations use absolute pressure (psia, referenced to zero vacuum): psig = psia − 14.69595 at sea level.
Verify SI prefixes before converting: 1 kPa = 1,000 Pa (0.14504 psi) and 1 MPa = 1,000,000 Pa (145.03774 psi)—omitting a prefix shifts the psi result by 1,000× or 1,000,000×.

faqs.question: How many psi are in 1 pascal?
faqs.answer: 1 pascal equals 0.00014504 psi (1 ÷ 6,894.75729). Conversely, 1 psi equals 6,894.75729 Pascals (about 6.895 kPa).

faqs.question: How to convert psia to psi (psig)?
faqs.answer: Everyday 'psi' on tire and compressor gauges refers to gauge pressure (psig). To convert absolute pressure (psia) to gauge pressure (psig) at sea level, subtract standard atmospheric pressure (14.69595 psi): psig = psia − 14.69595. At higher altitudes, subtract local barometric pressure.

faqs.question: How do I convert PSI to Pascals?
faqs.answer: Multiply pounds per square inch by 6,894.75729: Pa = psi × 6,894.75729. For example, 10 psi × 6,894.75729 = 68,947.57 Pa (68.95 kPa).

faqs.question: What is 100,000 Pascals (1 bar) in psi?
faqs.answer: 100,000 Pascals (100 kPa or 1 bar) equals 14.50377 psi.
